text: One email footer turned a tiny startup into a $400 million company.
say: One email footer turned a tiny startup into a four hundred million dollar company.

text: In 1996, two engineers launched Hotmail. Free email in any web browser.
say: In nineteen ninety-six, two engineers launched Hotmail. Free email in any web browser.

text: Back then, your email was usually tied to your internet provider.
The founders wanted billboards. An investor told them that was too expensive.
His idea? Put one line at the bottom of every single email.
PS: I love you. Get your free email at Hotmail.
say: P.S. I love you. Get your free email at Hotmail.

text: The founders hated it. They cut the I love you, but kept the link.
Now every email was a free ad, sent by a friend.
Signups exploded. By the end of 1997, Hotmail had over 9 million users.
say: Signups exploded. By the end of nineteen ninety-seven, Hotmail had over nine million users.

text: Then Microsoft bought it, reportedly for around $400 million.
say: Then Microsoft bought it, reportedly for around four hundred million dollars.

text: The lesson? Everything you send is marketing.
Your email signature, invoices, quotes. Put your website link on all of them.
Would you have kept the I love you? Follow for more Internet Stories.
